entry.title: How Origame Digital are channelling and defacing Lovecraft over a trilogy of "inherently indigenous" anti-fascist games
entry.summary:
Much like the H.P. Lovecraft novella it alternately riffs on and skewers, Penguin Colony takes you to an ancient alien city of crabby cuboid geometry and helical designs – comparable at a glance to Lovecraft's "terraces of every sort of provocative disproportion", but here given strangely everyday, anachronistic-seeming labels, such as "Downtown". Later, you're shown flashes of footage of the streets of Melbourne in Australia - developer Origame Digital's base of operations, and a city built on stolen Wurundjeri Woi-wurrung and Bunurong Boon Wurrung land.
When I first set foot in Downtown, in the unassuming body of a Rockhopper penguin, I thought the broad idea was to satirically redefine modern settlements built by European colonisers as Lovecraftian relics, intrusions from the cosmic beyond. This irony seems most pointed in sections where you steer a group of Māori characters, journeying south to prevent an expedition of German and British Nazi occultists from resurrecting a surviving elder being they call the "one true Aryan king". Playing as one of the Māori voyagers, you witness the cyclopean city as a realm of spectral high rises and square windows, rearing out of a swamp of blood and bone.

entry.title: USN-9090-1: Apache HTTP Server vulnerabilities
entry.summary:
Zhenpeng Lin discovered that Apache HTTP Server's mod_dav module incorrectly calculated memory sizes when handling WebDAV locks. An attacker with permission to create WebDAV locks could possibly use this issue to cause Apache HTTP Server to crash, resulting in a denial of service. (CVE-2026-42528)
It was discovered that Apache HTTP Server's mod_vhost_alias module incorrectly handled certain requests, leading to a one-byte stack buffer overflow. A remote attacker could possibly use this issue to cause Apache HTTP Server to crash, resulting in a denial of service, or possibly execute arbitrary code. (CVE-2026-109163)
It was discovered that Apache HTTP Server's mod_md module incorrectly handled certain conditions, leading to a NULL pointer dereference. An attacker could possibly use this issue to cause Apache HTTP Server to crash, resulting in a denial of service. This issue only affected Ubuntu 20.04 LTS, Ubuntu 22.04 LTS, Ubuntu 24.04 LTS, Ubuntu 26.04 LTS, and Ubuntu 26.10. (CVE-2026-106023)
It was discovered that Apache HTTP Server's mod_http2 module incorrectly handled certain request headers, leading to heap corruption. A remote attacker could possibly use this issue to cause Apache HTTP Server to crash, resulting in a denial of service, or possibly execute arbitrary code. This issue only affected Ubuntu 20.04 LTS, Ubuntu 22.04 LTS, Ubuntu 24.04 LTS, Ubuntu 26.04 LTS, and Ubuntu 26.10. (CVE-2026-119618)
Feliks Penconek, Yang Song, and JiaSheng He discovered that Apache HTTP Server could treat the target of some internal redirects from CGI programs as a CGI program. A remote attacker could possibly use this issue to execute arbitrary code. This issue only affected Ubuntu 26.04 LTS and Ubuntu 26.10. (CVE-2026-42356)

entry.title: There were 47 graphics chip makers in 1998. Where did they all go?

In 1998, 47 companies were designing or selling PC graphics, driving a market that hit 130 million units and outsold PCs themselves. entry.title: DigiCert: únik zákaznických údajů
entry.summary:
Digicert hlásí neoprávněné čtení archivních zákaznických údajů. Došlo k němu po migraci z února 2025, po níž se interní systém, dříve dostupný jen přes VPN, stal přístupným z internetu. Chyba v oprávněních umožnila nově vytvořeným účtům číst archivní záznamy. K přístupu k datům mělo dojít mezi 27. červnem a 2. červencem 2026. DigiCert neoprávněné čtení potvrdil až 19. října 2026. Problém zpočátku vyhodnotil jako tvorbu účtů, ne jako přístup k datům.
Dotčené údaje zahrnovaly jména, pracovní e-maily, telefonní čísla a obchodní adresy. U malé části záznamů byly také doklady, například pasy, řidičské průkazy nebo účty za služby. Počet zasažených lidí ani organizací zatím zveřejněn nebyl. DigiCert podle zpráv stále posuzuje, komu se týkaly doklady, a informuje dotčené zákazníky. DigiCert uvádí, že jeho certifikační služby, CertCentral, DigiCert ONE, přihlašovací údaje zákazníků ani vydané certifikáty zasaženy nebyly. Nebyly zaznamenány změny validací ani vydávání či rušení certifikátů. Kvůli tomuto incidentu tedy zákazníci nemají měnit aktivní certifikáty. DigiCert přístup uzavřel, vypnul samoobslužnou registraci a přidal další kontroly. Pokud jste DigiCertu posílali doklad totožnosti, ověřte u svého kontaktního zástupce, zda se vás incident týká. Zprávy, které se odvolávají na incident a žádají heslo, ověřovací kód nebo opětovné nahrání dokladu, si ověřte nezávisle přes svůj účet či známý kontakt — samotná oznámení neuvádějí úplný seznam zasažených.

entry.title: Airframe Ultra's PS1 cyberpunk city is an amazing tribute to G-Police and WipEout, and I wish you people would slow down to appreciate it
entry.summary:
I do not wish to "rule the streets" of Megacity West, dear creators of Airframe Ultra. I wish to be ravished by them, rubbing my face against the rusty corrugated metal of the shipping containers, and savouring the acid blue waters of the bay. I do not want to "become the one thing with freedom in a city of billions: A racer." I want to become the other thing with freedom in a city of billions: a person who slowly drives or – whisper it - walks around just looking at stuff, because gadzooks, this is one of the prettiest PS1 cyberpunk burgs I've laid eyes on.
Those eroded pastel chevrons. Those seductively wobbling vertices. That electric reef of a downtown backdrop, murderously luring your gaze from the on-coming trucks. That layer of invigorating crackle over everything. Every moment or so, I dismount from my hoverbike to inspect some concrete ruin I could swear I last saw in G-Police, or ponder the resemblance between a subway tunnel and WipEout 2097's Gare d'Europa. Then, somebody waps me in the skull with a stop sign at 300 kilometres an hour. But I was already stopped, frantic stranger! Your brutal poetic ironies are wasted on me.

Fellow contributor Sin Vega, in her 1.0 review, described it like this: "You have to build things to demolish things. That might be Workers & Resources in a nutshell. You're not managing budgets (money is exclusively for imports/exports), you're organising stuff." Now, having previously expanding out of the Soviet Republic and across the globe with the World Maps DLC, the next step for socialist citybuilding is, of course, space. Our Edwin outright predicted this two years ago, correctly calling that "the logical endgame here is to go to space." Good on him. Read more

entry.title: Arc Raiders devs Embark insist that using genAI for voice lines was necessary, as "actors would just go crazy if they had to read all of that"
entry.summary: Despite taking the voice performances of actors and feeding them into machines to spurt out AI-generated mimicry, Embark CCO Stefan Strandberg insists that "we are not in the industry of replacing actors." In a new video posted to the Arc Raiders channel focused on audio design, Strandberg refers back to the infamous use of genAI in Arc Raiders to generate voice lines based on real voice actors' performances, something which the game was heavily (and rightly) criticised for before and since its release. In that linked piece (thanks Oisin!), CEO Patrick Söderlund stated that they have been replacing lines that were originally generated with actual recorded lines, presumably because Arc Raiders has made quite a bit of money and now they feel that they can continue paying actors to record more lines, rather than just scraping their talents and avoiding the dreaded fee of paying professionals for their work. This choice already came after their previous game, The Finals, was heavily criticised for the exact same thing, which is just a fascinating series of decisions to consider. Read more

entry.summary: itch.io has unfortunately, much like Steam, long had an issue with genAI content being uploaded in droves, drowning out perfectly good games made by human hands.
